question:
Select the correct balanced chemical equation for the given reaction.

Magnesium(s) + Oxygen (g) → Magnesium oxide(s)
solution:
The correct answer is __**2Mg(s) + O2(g) → 2MgO(s).**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction between **magnesium metal** and **oxygen** produces **magnesium oxide**.
 
• This chemical reaction occurs when magnesium metal is burnt in the air.
 
• When magnesium and oxygen are combined, the resulting compound is called **magnesium oxide** and has the appearance of a **white powder**.
 
• In this reaction, two or more reactants combine to generate a single product, making it an example of a **combination reaction**, also called a **synthesis reaction.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Here,**2 magnesium atoms** react with **an oxygen** molecule to create **2 molecules of magnesium oxide** while also releasing **some heat**.
 
• **Magnesium** and **oxygen** are divalent elements which means elements with **2 valencies** are known as **divalent**.
 
• **What is known as a valency of an element?**
 
 
• **Valency** is the ability of an element to combine with other elements.
 
• One atom of **Chlorine (Cl)** combines with one atom of **Hydrogen (H)** to form a molecule of **hydrogen chloride**.
